title: Tracking follow-up of incidental imaging findings: a narrative review to inform a radiology department's choice
subtitle: Narrative review for the radiology quality committee, January 2027
statement: Radiology reports in the department often recommend follow-up imaging for incidental findings, but a spot check found completed follow-up within the recommended window for 94 of 200 patients and no evidence that the recommendation was seen for 41. The department must choose a tracking approach before the next budget round. A narrative review will describe how health systems track these recommendations, what completion they report, where the loop breaks and who is missed, so that the committee can choose on evidence.
whoAffected: Patients with incidental findings that need follow-up, especially patients without a family doctor and patients seen only in the emergency department; radiologists and ordering clinicians; and the quality committee that must choose and fund an approach.
whatHurts: Missed follow-up can delay the diagnosis of cancers in flagged lesions, as happened to two patients; unclear responsibility wastes clinician effort and leaves patients unaware of findings.
currentPractice: Recommendations are written as free text in the report and sent to the ordering clinician; there are no codes, no list of open recommendations, no navigator and no letters to patients.
whyNow: Two late cancer diagnoses, a spot check showing poor completion, and a budget decision in January 2027.
constraints: Three months for the review, reporting to the quality committee on 14 January 2027. Two radiologists and the hospital librarian share the work; no funding and no access to patient records for this review. English and French publications only.
patientCenteredGoal: Every patient with an incidental finding that needs follow-up learns about it and has the follow-up done in time, whoever ordered the original examination.
summary: Problem framed as a narrative review to inform the department's choice of a tracking approach for incidental finding follow-up.
